proposal.comment: [Playbook] Section 13 gives us an infringement remedy tied to a warranty breach but no express duty to defend and nothing for Garman's own misconduct, so we have added a defence and indemnity obligation covering IP infringement, breach of law, data/confidentiality incidents and gross negligence or wilful misconduct, with standard notice, control and cooperation mechanics. If needed, we can accept customary IP exclusions (our modifications, combinations or specifications) and a refund remedy as a fallback.

ops.text: In addition, Garman shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless Sparkling and its affiliates from and against any third party claim, and all resulting Losses, to the extent arising out of (a) an allegation that the Work, or any Improvements or Modifications thereto, infringes or misappropriates any intellectual property right; (b) Garman's breach of applicable law; (c) any unauthorized access to, or disclosure of, Sparkling's data or Confidential Information caused by Garman; or (d) Garman's gross negligence or wilful misconduct, including any resulting personal injury, death or damage to tangible property. Sparkling shall give Garman prompt written notice of any such claim, Garman shall have control of its defence and settlement (provided that no settlement imposing any liability or admission on Sparkling shall be made without Sparkling's prior written consent), and Sparkling shall provide reasonable cooperation at Garman's expense.

proposal.summary: Add Garman defence/indemnity for IP infringement, breach of law, data incidents and gross negligence or wilful misconduct, with standard claim procedure.

quote: Garman agrees to indemnify Sparkling and hold it harmless from any and all losses, damages and expenses including without limitation, court costs, arbitration fees, penalties, fines, amounts paid in settlement of claims and reasonable legal fees and expenses of investigation
rationale: Section 13 contains a Garman indemnity, but it is limited to breach of the IP ownership/non-infringement warranty and provides no express duty to defend, no coverage for Sparkling's affiliates, and nothing for Garman's breach of applicable law, unauthorized access to or disclosure of Sparkling data, or Garman's gross negligence or wilful misconduct (including resulting personal injury or property damage). There is no reciprocal Sparkling indemnity, and Section 15 already carves Section 13 out of the liability limitation, so the cap is not an issue. The inserted paragraph adds the missing indemnity heads and standard notice/control/cooperation mechanics, reaching the preferred position with a minimal addition to the existing section.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] Section 13 gives Garman ownership of everything "provided pursuant to the terms of this Agreement", including the Schedule "D" Modifications we commission and pay for, with no licence-back and no confirmation that our data stays ours. We have accepted that Garman keeps its platform (our preferred position is that we own work product created for us), so as a fallback we have carved out our data and materials and taken a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to the Modifications and Improvements, and confirmed there is no joint ownership.

ops.newText: including all related materials, logos, and names provided by Garman pursuant to the terms of this Agreement. Except for the licences granted to Sparkling under this Agreement, no title to the intellectual property in the Work is transferred to Sparkling by this Agreement.
ops.oldText: including all related materials, logos, and names provided pursuant to the terms of this Agreement. No title to the intellectual property in the Work is transferred to Sparkling by this Agreement.

ops.text: Notwithstanding the foregoing: (a) Sparkling retains all right, title and interest in and to Sparkling's data (including data converted under Section 4(b)) and all materials, information and specifications supplied by Sparkling, none of which is assigned or licensed to Garman except as reasonably necessary for Garman to perform its obligations under this Agreement; (b) Garman grants to Sparkling a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use the Modifications and the Improvements, and to modify them (itself or through a third party acting on its behalf), in the conduct of the business of Sparkling and its affiliated companies; and (c) nothing in this Agreement creates or is intended to create joint ownership of any intellectual property rights.

proposal.summary: Carve Sparkling's data and materials out of Garman's IP ownership claim, add a perpetual royalty-free licence to Modifications and Improvements we pay for, and bar joint ownership.

quote: Garman is the owner of all intellectual property rights in the Work (including any Improvements or Modifications thereto), including all related materials, logos, and names provided pursuant to the terms of this Agreement. No title to the intellectual property in the Work is transferred to Sparkling by this Agreement.
rationale: Section 13 vests ownership of all IP in the Work, including the Schedule "D" Modifications built and paid for by Sparkling, in Garman, with no licence-back beyond the narrow non-transferable object-code licence in Section 2 and no statement that Sparkling's data (including data converted under Section 4(b)) and supplied materials remain ours; the sweep-up for "all related materials... provided pursuant to the terms of this Agreement" could capture our own inputs. That fails the rule's requirement that we own what we pay for and assign nothing of ours to the Vendor. Because the bargain is an object-code licence to Garman's platform with escrow (Section 16), we took the fallback: Garman keeps its platform IP, we carve out our data and materials, take a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to the Modifications and Improvements, and rule out joint ownership.
ruleTitle: Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data

proposal.comment: [Playbook] Section 15 has no aggregate liability cap and is captioned as a limitation of Garman's liability only, so we have added a mutual cap at the greater of 12 months' fees or USD 1,000,000 in line with our position. Confidentiality, indemnification, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement sit outside the cap, and Sparkling's fee payment obligations are not subject to it; a straight mutual 12 months' fees cap is our fallback.

ops.newText: Except for Excluded Claims, each party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of (a) the fees paid or payable by Sparkling under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the event giving rise to the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000. "Excluded Claims" means a party's breach of Sections 13 or 14 or of its other confidentiality, data protection or security obligations, its indemnification obligations, its gross negligence, wilful misconduct or fraud, and its infringement of the other party's intellectual property rights. The limitations of liability in this Section 15 shall not apply to Excluded Claims, and Sparkling's obligation to pay fees due under this Agreement shall not be treated as damages subject to the cap.
ops.oldText: The limitation of liability in this Section 15 shall not apply to breaches of Sections 13 and 14.

proposal.summary: Add a mutual aggregate liability cap (greater of 12 months' fees or USD 1,000,000) with uncapped Excluded Claims, and make the section heading mutual.

quote: The exclusive remedy of either party in a claim against the other under this Agreement shall be the recovery of its direct damages. In no event shall either party be liable to the other for the recovery of any special, indirect or consequential damages even if the defendant party had been advised of the possibility of such damages including but not limited to lost profits, lost revenues, failure to realize expected savings, loss of data and loss of use.
rationale: Section 15 contains only a mutual exclusion of indirect/consequential damages and an exclusive-remedy statement; there is no aggregate monetary cap at all, and the caption presents the section as a limitation of Garman's liability only. The playbook requires a mutual cap at the greater of 12 months' fees or USD 1,000,000, with uncapped carve-outs. The existing carve-out reaches only Sections 13 and 14 and does not expressly cover gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, data protection/security or IP infringement, and Sparkling's payment obligations are not excluded from the cap. Redline adds the mutual cap with an Excluded Claims definition (preserving the Section 13/14 carve-out) and makes the heading mutual; fallback is a plain mutual 12 months' fees cap with carve-outs for indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct.
ruleTitle: Limitation of liability — cap, mutuality and carve-outs

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have replaced the blanket mutual assignment bar so that we may assign to an affiliate or to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets without consent (including the licence), while Garman's assignment still needs our consent (not unreasonably withheld) and may never be to our competitor. We have also confirmed that a change of control of Sparkling is not an assignment and gives Garman no termination or re-pricing right; if helpful, we can accept a mutual notice-based successor right with consent for other assignments not unreasonably withheld.

ops.newText: (d) Notwithstanding Section 2 and Section 3(c), Sparkling may assign this Agreement, and the licence granted under it, without the consent of Garman, to an affiliate of Sparkling or to a successor in connection with a merger, acquisition, reorganization or sale of all or substantially all of its assets or of the business to which this Agreement relates. Garman may not assign this Agreement or any rights and obligations under this Agreement without the prior written consent of Sparkling (which shall not be unreasonably withheld), and in no event to a competitor of Sparkling. Any other assignment by either party requires the prior written consent of the other party, which shall not be unreasonably withheld. No change of control of Sparkling shall constitute an assignment of this Agreement or entitle Garman to terminate, suspend or re-price this Agreement or the licence.
ops.oldText: (d) Neither party may assign this Agreement or any rights and obligations under this Agreement to any third party without the written consent of the other party.

proposal.summary: Add affiliate/successor assignment carve-out for Sparkling, qualify Garman's assignment rights, and confirm no change-of-control exit or re-pricing.

quote: (d) Neither party may assign this Agreement or any rights and obligations under this Agreement to any third party without the written consent of the other party.
rationale: Section 20(d) imposes a blanket consent requirement on assignment with no affiliate or M&A carve-out for Sparkling and no reasonableness standard, which is our walk-away position; it is reinforced by Section 3(c) (no assignment except as authorized by Garman in writing) and the "non-transferable" licence in Section 2. Nothing gives Garman a change-of-control termination right, but the absence of any change-of-control language leaves our reorganisations exposed to being treated as an assignment. The redline adds the affiliate/successor carve-out for us, keeps Garman's assignment subject to our consent (not unreasonably withheld) and off-limits to our competitors, and confirms that a change of control of Sparkling is not an assignment and triggers no Garman termination or re-pricing right.

quote: Garman hereby grants to Sparkling, for the use of Sparkling and affiliated companies of Sparkling operating at Authorized Locations, a non-transferable and non-exclusive licence to use: (i) the Software, safely in executable object code format, at each AS400 at each of the Authorized Locations; and (ii) the Documentation.
rationale: No exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation is imposed on Sparkling (Customer). The only uses of "exclusive" are (i) the non-exclusive licence grant in Section 2 (p0028), (ii) the "exclusive remedy" limitation in Section 15 (p0105), (iii) the non-exclusive escrow licence in Section 16 (p0115), and (iv) non-exclusive jurisdiction in the general provisions (p0146) — none of which restrict our freedom to source from other suppliers. The restrictions on Sparkling in Section 3 (p0030-p0037) are limited to copying, assignment, reverse engineering and scope-of-use covenants, with no covenant against procuring competing software or services from third parties. Maintenance and Support (Section 10, p0065 et seq.) obliges Garman to provide services on a renewable one-year term but does not require Sparkling to source support, Improvements or future modules solely from Garman, and Fees (Section 11, p0084) contains no minimum-purchase or requirements commitment. Searches for "sole", "requirements", "purchase", "procure", "supplier", "competing" and "exclusivity" returned no exclusive-dealing language. The Agreement therefore meets the preferred position and no redline is needed.

quote: (b) Sparkling may terminate this Agreement at any time upon ninety (90) calendar days written notice to Garman. If Sparkling terminates this Agreement pursuant to this Section 17(b), Sparkling shall cease using the Software at the end of the ninety (90) day notice period, and shall certify to Garman within thirty (30) calendar days of termination that Sparkling has destroyed or has returned to Garman all Software, Documentation and Codes.
rationale: The Agreement contains no liquidated damages, penalty, forfeiture or minimum-fee provision payable by Sparkling (the customer). Section 11 obliges Sparkling only to pay fees per the Fee Schedule; there is no late-payment interest or penalty. Section 17(b) permits Sparkling to terminate for convenience on 90 days' notice with no termination fee or accelerated/remaining-term payment, and Section 17 default termination by Sparkling actually converts the licence to perpetual and requires Garman to refund prepaid fees for services not rendered. Sections 3, 9 and 19 impose no monetary penalties on Sparkling. Section 15 confirms each party's remedy is direct damages only, excluding consequential loss. Any LD-type amounts run in our favour, which the playbook treats as compliant, so no redline is required.
ruleTitle: Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have extended the grant to contractors acting on our behalf (affiliates are already covered) and made the licence transferable, notwithstanding Sections 3(c) and 20(d), to a successor of our business, since our playbook requires the licence to cover affiliates and contractors and to survive an internal reorganisation or M&A transaction. If Garman prefers, we can accept adding affiliates/contractors on written notice to Garman.

ops.newText: for the use of Sparkling, affiliated companies of Sparkling and contractors acting on Sparkling's behalf, in each case operating at Authorized Locations, a non-exclusive licence, which Sparkling may transfer (notwithstanding Sections 3(c) and 20(d)) to a successor to its business by way of merger, acquisition or sale of all or substantially all of its assets, to use
ops.oldText: for the use of Sparkling and affiliated companies of Sparkling operating at Authorized Locations, a non-transferable and non-exclusive licence to use

proposal.summary: Extend licence to contractors acting for Sparkling and permit transfer to a successor

quote: Garman hereby grants to Sparkling, for the use of Sparkling and affiliated companies of Sparkling operating at Authorized Locations, a non-transferable and non-exclusive licence to use
rationale: The grant covers Sparkling's affiliated companies (at Authorized Locations) and is perpetual so long as fees are paid (§17(a)), and converts to a fee-free perpetual licence on Garman default (§17(c)), so it is not revocable at will. However, it omits contractors acting on our behalf and is expressly "non-transferable", with §3(c) and §20(d) barring assignment or transfer without Garman's written consent, so the licence would not survive an M&A transaction. We therefore added contractors and a successor-transfer right in the grant clause.

quote: (g) not use the Work to act as a service bureau in whole or in part, for any other Person, except for any affiliate of Sparkling operating at the Authorized Locations.
rationale: The Agreement contains no non-compete or field-of-use covenant binding Sparkling. Section 3 (Restrictions on Use) is limited to ordinary licence-scope restrictions on the Software and Documentation (no copying beyond backup, no reverse engineering, no sublicence/assignment, no service bureau use of the Work); none of these limit the businesses Sparkling may operate or the routing products it may buy or build. Section 19 is a mutual non-solicitation of employees (one year, both parties), not a non-compete, and Section 20 (General Matters) contains only boilerplate. Text searches for "compet", "develop" and "exclusiv" surface no competing-products, territory or field-of-use restriction on our party. Consistent with the playbook preferred position, no redline is required.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have shortened our convenience-termination notice to 30 days and confirmed a pro-rata refund of prepaid (including maintenance) fees, consistent with our position that we can exit on 30 days' notice without penalty. If 30 days is difficult operationally, we can accept 60 days' notice provided the pro-rata refund of prepaid fees remains.

ops.newText: Sparkling may terminate this Agreement or any part of the Maintenance Services for convenience at any time upon thirty (30) calendar days written notice to Garman, without penalty or early-termination charge, and Garman shall refund to Sparkling any prepaid fees (including prepaid maintenance fees) for the period after the effective date of termination. If Sparkling terminates this Agreement pursuant to this Section 17(b), Sparkling shall cease using the Software at the end of the thirty (30) day notice period,
ops.oldText: Sparkling may terminate this Agreement at any time upon ninety (90) calendar days written notice to Garman. If Sparkling terminates this Agreement pursuant to this Section 17(b), Sparkling shall cease using the Software at the end of the ninety (90) day notice period,

proposal.summary: Customer convenience termination reduced to 30 days' notice with pro-rata refund of prepaid fees.

quote: (b) Sparkling may terminate this Agreement at any time upon ninety (90) calendar days written notice to Garman.
rationale: Section 17(b) gives us a convenience right, and Garman has no convenience right (Section 17(c) termination is only for insolvency or uncured default), so the vendor-side test is satisfied. However, the notice period is 90 days (only fallback-level) and, in a perpetual licence with annually prepaid maintenance fees (Section 10, 17(a)), nothing requires Garman to refund prepaid fees for the post-termination period — an effective early-exit penalty. Our preferred position is 30 days' notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees, so we redlined 17(b) accordingly and offered 60 days as a fallback if the refund is preserved.

quote: (e) not use the Work except as authorized herein;
rationale: Searches for audit, inspect, verify, examine, records, premises, monitor and compliance across the whole agreement return no verification or audit right exercisable by Garman against Sparkling. Section 3 (Restrictions on Use) — the usual home for a usage-verification right — imposes only substantive use restrictions with no inspection or system-access mechanism, and Section 20 (General Matters) contains only time-of-essence and notice provisions. The only examination right in the document (p0114, escrow materials) runs in our favour, exercisable by Sparkling using independent experts. Because the playbook position is a limit on audits of our usage, the total absence of any such vendor right is better than the preferred position, so no redline is warranted; adding audit machinery would create a right Garman does not currently have.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have replaced Nova Scotia law and the non-exclusive Nova Scotia courts with New York law and the exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts in New York County, which is our standard governing-law position. If helpful, we can accept Delaware, California, or the laws of England and Wales with the courts of London as a fallback.

ops.newText: the laws of the State of New York. All disputes under this Agreement shall be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts located in New York County, New York.
ops.oldText: the laws of Nova Scotia and the laws of Canada applicable in Nova Scotia. All disputes under this Agreement shall be subject to the non-exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of Nova Scotia.

proposal.summary: Change governing law and venue from Nova Scotia to New York with exclusive New York County courts

quote: (h) This Agreement shall be governed by the laws of Nova Scotia and the laws of Canada applicable in Nova Scotia. All disputes under this Agreement shall be subject to the non-exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of Nova Scotia.
rationale: The governing-law clause selects Nova Scotia law and the non-exclusive jurisdiction of the Nova Scotia courts, which is outside the accepted list (New York, Delaware, California, or England and Wales). Nova Scotia is also not our home jurisdiction, so this is a counterparty-favorable forum. There is no arbitration clause, so the court-based forum itself is acceptable; only the jurisdiction words and forum need to change. Redline moves the clause to New York law with exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts in New York County, per the preferred position, leaving the balance of the sentence intact.

quote: Sparkling shall pay the fees as set out in the Fee Schedule in accordance with the terms of this Agreement and the Fee Schedule.
rationale: Searches for MFN/pricing-parity language ("no less favourable", "favourable/favorable", "price", "customers", "third part") returned no parity or price-matching provision. The fees clause (§11) simply requires payment per the Fee Schedule, and the maintenance provisions (§10 and continuation) contain only Garman-side service obligations and limited chargeable-repair exceptions; §20 general matters has no parity term. There is therefore no obligation on Sparkling to extend Garman terms no less favourable than those given to third parties or to match third-party offers, so the preferred position (no MFN burdening Customer) is met and no redline is required. An MFN in our favour is optional and not mandated by the rule.

quote: (b) Sparkling may terminate this Agreement at any time upon ninety (90) calendar days written notice to Garman.
rationale: The Agreement contains no minimum purchase commitment, take-or-pay, shortfall or volume-commitment language. Fees are payable only "as set out in the Fee Schedule" for the licensed Software and Authorized Locations actually taken (§ 11, § 2), and maintenance runs on a "renewable one-year term" (§ 10) rather than a multi-year committed spend. Sparkling also has an at-will exit on 90 days' notice under § 17(b), and the license continues only "as long as fees are paid", so there is no locked-in spend. The § 3 restrictions are ordinary IP/scope-of-use limits, not volume caps or purchase obligations. This meets the preferred position (usage/ordered services only); no redline required. Note only that the Fee Schedule (Schedule "A") is not included in the reviewed text and should be checked to confirm it contains no minimum quantities or non-refundable multi-year prepayments.
ruleTitle: Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We cannot accept a no-hire covering all of the other party's employees, so we have replaced it with a mutual non-solicitation limited to individuals directly involved in the services, running 12 months from the end of their involvement, with the customary carve-outs for general advertising and unsolicited approaches. Our preferred position is no such restriction on us at all, but we are content with this narrowed mutual formulation.

ops.newText: During the term of this Agreement and for a period of twelve (12) months after the end of an individual's involvement in the provision of services under this Agreement, neither party will, and neither party will permit its affiliates to, directly solicit for employment any employee of the other party who was directly involved in the provision of services under this Agreement. This Section does not prohibit either party from hiring any person, and does not apply to general advertisements or other recruitment efforts not specifically targeted at the other party's personnel, or to any person who approaches a party on an unsolicited basis or who responds to such general recruitment.
ops.oldText: During the term of this Agreement and for a period of one year thereafter, both parties agree not to hire or allow its respective affiliates to hire any employee of the other party, or any person who was an employee of the other party during the previous six months and who was directly involved in the provision of services under this Agreement.

proposal.summary: Convert mutual no-hire into a narrow 12-month mutual non-solicit limited to personnel involved in the services, with general-advertising and unsolicited-approach carve-outs

quote: During the term of this Agreement and for a period of one year thereafter, both parties agree not to hire or allow its respective affiliates to hire any employee of the other party, or any person who was an employee of the other party during the previous six months and who was directly involved in the provision of services under this Agreement.
rationale: Section 19 binds us (mutually) with a no-hire, not merely a non-solicit: it prohibits hiring "any employee of the other party" for the term plus one year, with no limitation to personnel involved in the services in its first limb and no carve-out for general advertisements or unsolicited approaches. No-hire provisions covering all of the counterparty's personnel are a walk-away under the playbook. Since the restriction is mutual and part of the existing bargain, we narrow to the fallback rather than delete: a 12-month non-solicit running from the end of an individual's involvement, limited to personnel directly involved in the services, with general-advertising and unsolicited-approach carve-outs and express confirmation that hiring is not prohibited. Survival in Section 18 remains acceptable for the narrowed clause.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] Section 10 makes maintenance a "renewable one-year term" without specifying how renewal happens or limiting the renewal fee, so we have added 12-month renewals that we can decline on 30 days' notice, a 60-day reminder from Garman, and an uplift cap of the lesser of CPI and 3%. If the cap is an issue we can accept a 5% ceiling with a 60-day non-renewal notice window.

ops.newText: For an initial one-year term commencing upon the Maintenance Commencement Date and for successive twelve (12) month renewal terms thereafter (provided that Sparkling may elect not to renew by written notice to Garman given at least thirty (30) calendar days before the end of the then-current term, and Garman shall notify Sparkling of the upcoming renewal at least sixty (60) calendar days before the end of the then-current term), subject to payment of maintenance fees in accordance with the Fee Schedule (which fees shall not increase for any renewal term by more than the lesser of the increase in the Consumer Price Index over the prior term and three percent (3%))
ops.oldText: For a renewable one-year term commencing upon the Maintenance Commencement Date, subject to payment of maintenance fees in accordance with the Fee Schedule

proposal.summary: Add renewal mechanics and a cap on maintenance fee uplift for renewal terms of Maintenance Services

quote: For a renewable one-year term commencing upon the Maintenance Commencement Date, subject to payment of maintenance fees in accordance with the Fee Schedule but without additional fees or charges, Garman shall provide the following Maintenance Services:
rationale: Maintenance runs for a "renewable one-year term" but the Agreement never states how renewal occurs, gives no non-renewal notice window or renewal reminder, and (with Sections 11 and 17 simply pointing to the Fee Schedule) leaves renewal-term maintenance fees uncapped. The playbook requires renewals to be easy to exit and predictably priced, so we added 12-month renewal terms that Sparkling may decline on 30 days' notice, a 60-day Garman reminder, and a cap of the lesser of CPI and 3% on any renewal uplift; fallback is a 60-day window and 5% cap.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have added a transition and data-return provision at Section 17(d) so that, on any expiry or termination, Garman gives us up to six months of transition assistance at its then-current rates and returns our data in a machine-readable format within thirty days before certifying deletion; the agreement currently addresses return of Garman's Software but says nothing about our own data or an orderly exit. If six months is an issue we can accept ninety days of assistance, provided the thirty-day data export remains.

ops.text: (d) Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Garman shall (1) at Sparkling's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Garman's then-current rates; (2) within thirty (30) calendar days of Sparkling's request, return to Sparkling all of Sparkling's data in its possession or control in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (3) thereafter delete Sparkling's data from its systems and certify such deletion to Sparkling in writing.

proposal.summary: Insert Section 17(d) requiring Garman to provide transition assistance and return/delete Sparkling's data on termination, and add it to the survival list.

quote: Sparkling shall cease using the Software at the end of the ninety (90) day notice period, and shall certify to Garman within thirty (30) calendar days of termination that Sparkling has destroyed or has returned to Garman all Software, Documentation and Codes.
rationale: Section 17 addresses only Sparkling's obligations to stop using and return Garman's Software, Documentation and Codes; there is no reciprocal obligation on Garman to provide transition assistance, return Sparkling's data (converted and hosted under Section 4/Schedule D) in a usable format, or certify deletion. The only data-return language is in Section 8, which applies solely if Sparkling rejects the Software during acceptance, and the escrow in Section 16 is at most a partial substitute. We therefore insert a new Section 17(d) with six months of transition assistance at then-current rates, a 30-day machine-readable data return and post-return deletion certification, and add it to the Section 18 survival list so it operates after termination.
ruleTitle: Post-termination transition assistance and data return

proposal.comment: [Playbook] Section 12 gives a one-year Software conformance warranty but no stated warranty remedy, no services warranty and no malicious-code or legal-compliance warranty, and repair is currently available only under the paid maintenance arrangement in Section 10. We have added a professional and workmanlike services warranty plus a repair/replace-then-refund remedy, consistent with our standard warranty position; if helpful we can accept a 90-day services warranty period.

ops.text: Garman further warrants that (a) all services provided under this Agreement, including installation, data conversion, training and Maintenance Services, shall be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; (b) the Software and such services shall comply with all applicable laws; and (c) the Software shall not contain any virus, disabling device or other malicious code. Sparkling's remedy for breach of the warranties in this Section 12 shall be, at Garman's option, re-performance, repair or replacement of the non-conforming Software or services at no charge to Sparkling, and if Garman fails to do so within 30 business days of written notice, a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Software or services. The warranties in this Section 12 are in addition to, and not limited or displaced by, the Maintenance Services described in Section 10.

proposal.summary: Add services warranty, malicious code and legal compliance warranties, and an express repair/replace/refund remedy to Section 12.

quote: For the acceptance period and for a period of one year from the Maintenance Commencement Date, and thereafter for as long as the Software is covered by Maintenance Services and is used by Sparkling in accordance with this Agreement, Garman warrants that the Software shall perform in conformance with the Specifications in all material respects.
rationale: The Software conformance warranty period (one year from the Maintenance Commencement Date, extended while maintenance continues) meets the preferred 12-month position, and there is no implied-warranty disclaimer or "AS IS" language anywhere in the agreement, so the disclaimer does not swallow the express warranty (Section 15 limits damages only). However, the warranty is incomplete: (i) no remedy is attached to it — repair is available only as a Maintenance Service under Section 10 (p0077), which is fee-bearing and could lapse, and the Section 7/8 refund is confined to the acceptance period; (ii) there is no professional and workmanlike warranty covering installation, data conversion, training and maintenance services; and (iii) there are no malicious code or legal compliance warranties. We therefore insert a single paragraph in Section 12 adding the services warranty, malicious code/compliance warranties and a repair/replace-then-refund remedy, and confirming the warranty is not displaced by Section 10 maintenance.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] Garman installs and maintains the Software at our Authorized Locations and converts our data, so we need it to carry standard cover. We have added a short insurance covenant (commercial general liability USD 1M/2M, E&O USD 2M, cyber USD 5M where our data is processed, plus statutory workers' compensation and certificates on request); we can accept E&O of USD 1M and cyber of USD 2M as a fallback.

ops.text: (k) Garman shall maintain, at its own expense, throughout the term of this Agreement and for one (1) year thereafter: commercial general liability insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate; professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000; where Garman processes Sparkling's data, cyber and privacy liability insurance of not less than USD 5,000,000; and workers' compensation insurance as required by applicable law. Garman shall provide Sparkling with certificates of insurance evidencing such coverage on request.

proposal.summary: Insert vendor insurance covenant as new § 20(k)

quote: (j) This Agreement constitutes the entire Agreement between the parties with respect to its subject matter, and this Agreement supersedes all prior understandings, representations, negotiations and communications between the parties, oral and written.
rationale: The Agreement contains no insurance clause (search for "insurance" returns nothing) even though Garman installs and maintains the Software at Sparkling's Authorized Locations, provides on-site training and converts Sparkling's data. Playbook requires standard vendor cover, so we insert a short insurance covenant as new § 20(k) in General Matters after the entire-agreement subsection.
